premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and this killed us: the HDPE cap-to-board bond delaminated after real transit vibration and repeated stacking loads within the first few weeks of sales, and a viral 'this fake-rated protector fell apart' video tanked the rating before review count ever recovered.
premortem.mitigation: Validate the cap-to-board joint (mechanical crimp or structural hot-melt, not a light adhesive dab) with the same test rig used for the slot-tab retention test, adding a vibration/transit-simulation pass before sign-off.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Incremental scope added to the already-budgeted test rig line, not a new fixture.

premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and this killed us: a second factory in the same trade-show network copied the printed-spec-plus-blue-cap look within 90 days and undercut us at 60% of price, and the brief's own LOW-BARRIER-to-entry tag turned out to be exactly right.
premortem.mitigation: Keep the hero deboss/hot-stamp mold (I1) as the differentiator held back until v2, own the tool rather than share it across factories, and lean on the weight-match card + belly-band system as a harder-to-clone service layer than a cap shape alone.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Genuinely zero - this is a sequencing/IP-ownership decision (deferring I1, not sharing tooling), not a new purchase.

premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and this killed us: the rigid-mailer packaging landed a few millimetres over the small-standard size-tier line and the FBA fee jumped a full tier, quietly erasing the margin the base-case numbers assumed.
premortem.mitigation: Lock external packed dimensions with a 5mm safety margin under the small-standard threshold at DFM sign-off, confirmed on 3 physical production samples with calipers before committing to the full production run.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Trivial - a dimensional-check step folded into the existing QC pass.

premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and this killed us: the China-origin tariff on HTS 4819 goods moved again (as it already did once in Feb 2026 per scout's trend note), and the true classification for this mixed corrugated+HDPE product turned out to sit under a higher-duty heading than the assumed 4819.10.
premortem.mitigation: Get a binding CBP classification ruling on the true HTS heading for the mixed-material product before committing to the full 1,500-unit MOQ, and hold a cash buffer sized to the widened duty+tariff range (up to 62% of EXW in the high case).

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Typical cost of a binding ruling request via a customs broker.

premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and this killed us: Amazon flagged the 'curbside recyclable' claim on the belly-band as unsubstantiated and suppressed the listing pending a policy review, right as the launch ad budget was spent driving traffic to it.
premortem.mitigation: Keep the sustainability claim generic and verifiable (standard OCC/kraft recycling stream, no numeric recycled-content % since no supplier certificate exists yet, per innovaty's own rejected_claims list), and route final packaging copy through Amazon's claims-review guidance before going live.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Compliance copy review, no structural change needed.

premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and this killed us: with zero visible reviews for months, buyer after buyer hit the exact 'is this flimsy junk from an unknown brand' wall (fear rank 5, N3) and bought the 100-pack with 4,000 reviews sitting right next to us instead - review velocity never crossed the chasm.
premortem.mitigation: Enroll in Vine and run a launch-week giveaway to a reseller/small-shipper micro-influencer audience, targeting 15+ reviews by week 8 post-launch rather than waiting on organic velocity; do not treat ad spend alone as a substitute for review count.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: ~30-60 seeded units at landed cost plus Vine enrollment fee; matches the review-seeding NRE line in tooling_and_nre.

premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and this killed us: a competitor or an independent reviewer crush-tested the board and showed it doesn't actually hold to ECT-32, and the brief's own flagged risk - a supplier quietly substituting a lower linerboard grade - turned out to be exactly what happened, which is fatal for a product whose entire pitch is 'you can trust this number.'
premortem.mitigation: Require a mill certificate confirming true ECT-32 linerboard on every PO (not just the first sample run), keep a batch-traceable retained sample from every production lot, and be ready to publish the certificate if the claim is ever publicly challenged.

regulatory: No government certification applies - ECT is an industry test spec (TAPPI/ASTM-style edge crush test), not a regulatory mark; listing and pack copy must say 'stated' or 'rated to,' never 'certified.'
Prop 65 labeling review recommended for the HDPE components as a precaution, even though virgin HDPE resin is not expected to contain a listed substance.
No CPSC/magnet scrutiny applicable - no magnets, no child-directed marketing in this product.
Standard FBA packaging/labeling and size-tier compliance only for a passive corrugated+HDPE shipping accessory.
three_sentences_to_founder: Ship the base set first - I2's weight-match card, I3's blue caps, I4's longer wings, I5's self-locking fold - at $13.99-$16.79 (base $15.49): landed cost runs about $2.78 at the base case ($1.39-$5.47 range) against $6,650-$24,000 of tooling and launch NRE, none of which requires the hero mold - but the two problem clusters this whole plan targets (corner crush from a thickness mismatch, confusing duty-tier picks) are scout's own inferred read on SKU-tier proliferation, not mined from real one-star reviews, so a review-mining pass once web access is unblocked should land before or alongside committing the full tooling spend, not after.

The debossed 'ECT-32' hero cap (I1) waits for v2, priced at an extra $1,500-$6,000 in tooling alone - it's a stretch call, not a must, because the printed card, belly-band and hard-case photo already give buyers the 'visible reason' they need to pay near the top of the price band without it.

The two things actually worth funding on day one are review-seeding (zero reviews is the buyer's #1 unanswerable fear, roughly 45% chance it stalls month-6 volume, $300-$1,200 to mitigate) and a mill certificate on every PO to back the ECT-32 claim (roughly 18% chance of a fatal spec-integrity challenge if unverified, $100-$500 to mitigate).
